summary: The study describes the growth of ultrathin CdTe quantum wells (UTQWs) within ZnTe barriers using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) on GaAs(001) substrates. The process involved alternating exposure of the substrate to Cd and Te fluxes, with two samples grown at different temperatures (270°C and 290°C) resulting in 2 ML and 4 ML thick QWs, respectively. The optical properties were analyzed using photoluminescence (PL) and photoreectance (PR) measurements, revealing insights into the structural and optical behavior of the CdTe QWs.
evidence: Ultrathin quantum wells (UTQWs) of CdTe within ZnTe barriers were successfully grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) on GaAs(001) substrates. ALE growth of CdTe was performed by alternate exposure of the substrate surface to individual fluxes of Cd and Te. Two different samples with 2 monolayer (ML) (substrate temperature Ts = 270°C) and 4 ML (Ts = 290°C) CdTe QWs were grown. Room temperature (RT) photoreectance (PR) spectra showed contributions from the CdTe UTQWs, the ZnTe barriers, and the GaAs substrate.
